bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for strategic renovations and new builds; maintaining strong net cash position (₹59 Cr as of Mar 2026); no dividends or buybacks disclosed
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delays in new project completions; regulatory approvals for expansions; geopolitical disruptions impacting travel; monsoon-related seasonal volatility; competition from international luxury chains
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Despite FY26 revenue decline YoY (-6%), EIH maintained EBITDA margin and PAT resilience due to premium pricing power and cost discipline — indicating strong brand pricing leverage not seen in peers.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The deck runs a slide titled "Strong Balance Sheet": Fund Position rose to Rs.308 crores at Mar 31, 2026 from Rs.270 crores (Mar 31, 2025), Rs.193 crores (Mar 31, 2024) and Rs.82 crores (Mar 31, 2022).
- Net Worth reached Rs.602 crores at Mar 31, 2026 versus Rs.537 crores (Mar 31, 2025) and Rs.319 crores (Mar 31, 2021), a continuous build across all seven dates shown.
- Leverage is effectively nil — full-year Finance Costs of Rs.0.5 crores (FY26) against EBITDA of Rs.138.3 crores — so the Vishakhapatnam build and Jaipur renovation are being funded from an accumulating internal fund position rather than debt.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Room Revenue: Corporate (dominant), Leisure, MICE; Q4FY26 RevPAR: ₹14,093 (vs industry ₹7,308); Occupancy: 86% in March FY26; ARR: ₹21,000+ in peak months
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Operates under the Oberoi group's two brands — The Oberoi (Rajvilas Jaipur, Cecil Shimla) at the luxury end and Trident (Agra, Jaipur, Udaipur, Bhubaneshwar, Chennai) in the upscale segment; investor contact is routed through isdho@oberoigroup.com.
- A dedicated slide claims "RevPAR Growth of EIH Associated Hotels consistently higher than industry", charting EIHA FY24/FY25/FY26 monthly RevPAR against the corresponding industry lines (source: HVS Anarock, April 2026).
- The deck frames the industry backdrop as rate-led rather than occupancy-led: FY25-26 industry ARR Rs.8,700-8,900 (+9-10% vs PY) and RevPAR Rs.5,650-5,850 (+10-12%) on occupancy of 63%-65% (+0-1 pp), described as "strong rate-led growth with ARR growing at ~10%".
- Demand mix commentary is that "corporate, weddings and MICE demand remained resilient" even as Q4 air-traffic growth stayed subdued (March at ~1% YoY) and March softened against a strong February base.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin: 36.0% (FY26), down from 35.7% (FY25) on higher revenue; EBITDA per available room: ₹1,762 (FY26) vs ₹1,618 (FY25); cost control maintained despite inflation
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Focus on completing renovations (Jaipur) and launching new properties (Udaipur expansion, Vishakhapatnam) to drive future RevPAR growth; maintaining premium pricing power and operational efficiency.
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: Trident Udaipur expansion (+10 keys), Trident Vishakhapatnam (new 125-key hotel), Banquet expansion at Trident Agra; pipeline adds ~262 keys over next 2-3 years
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: EIH Associated Hotels is India's premier luxury hotel operator with consistent RevPAR outperformance, driven by premium brand equity and resilient corporate/MICE demand. Despite FY26 revenue softening due to one-off closures and macro headwinds, the company is positioned for strong recovery via strategic renovations and new openings in high-growth corridors.

open.item: Board recommended a dividend of Rs. 3.5 (35%) per equity share for FY 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.
Construction of a new 125-room, five-star beachfront Trident Hotel in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, strategically located near the upcoming Bhogapuram International Airport.
Comprehensive renovation of 127 rooms at Trident Jaipur, underway to enrich the guest experience while preserving the property's character.
Addition of 10 keys at Trident Udaipur to strengthen ability to cater to growing leisure, wedding and event demand.
Development of a new banquet facility at Trident Agra to strengthen the hotel's appeal for weddings, events and social gatherings.
Commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 across the portfolio.
Additional environmentally conscious practices under the 'Elements by Oberoi' sustainability brand philosophy are planned for rollout in coming financial years.

Development of a 125-room Trident hotel in Visakhapatnam in partnership with the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (APTDC), on a 40-acre beachfront site comprising a luxury resort and an integrated convention centre; groundbreaking occurred in late 2024.

Trident Udaipur is expanding accommodation with the addition of 10 luxury tents overlooking Lake Pichola, a children's activity centre and a second pool, complementing the existing inventory of 142 rooms and suites.
Comprehensive renovation programme underway at the 127-room Trident Jaipur to re-position the hotel and strengthen its positioning as a leading luxury destination.
Trident Agra is expanding events and conferencing capabilities through development of a new banquet facility to host weddings, social celebrations and corporate events.

Development of a 125-room, five-star beachfront Trident Hotel in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, in partnership with the Andhra Pradesh Tourism Development Corporation (APTDC) on a 40-acre beachfront site near the upcoming Bhogapuram International Airport, comprising a luxury resort and an integrated convention centre; groundbreaking occurred in late 2024 and construction is progressing.

drhp.business: EIH Associated Hotels Limited is a luxury hospitality company that owns and operates seven hotels across India under the Oberoi Hotels & Resorts and Trident Hotels brands, providing accommodation, food & beverage and allied hospitality services (spa, banquets/MICE, laundry, guest transfers, loyalty programmes) to individual and group leisure travellers, corporate clients, travel agencies and event managers. The company commenced its journey in 1983 as Pleasant Hotels Limited and today operates across key business and leisure destinations in India.

risks.note: Operation Sindoor in Q1 FY26 and continuing geopolitical tensions/conflict in West Asia in Q4 FY26 contributed to heightened uncertainty; management flags that resulting volatility may affect operating costs, business sentiment and travel demand in FY 2026-27, particularly inbound foreign tourism and corporate travel during the historic peak H2 period, with rising fuel prices potentially influencing airline capacity, airfares and travel patterns.
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and aviation disruption in West Asia

risks.note: The Code on Wages 2019, Industrial Relations Code 2020, Code on Social Security 2020 and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code 2020 required the Company to recognise an incremental obligation of Rs. 32.82 Million towards increased employee benefit liabilities relating to past service (booked as an Exceptional Item); the Company continues to monitor further rules and clarifications that could add incremental cost.
risks.risk: Regulatory cost risk from India's new Labour Codes

risks.note: Revenue declined 5.6% y-o-y to Rs. 4,031.96 Million, EBITDA fell 4.6%, profit before tax fell 5.0% and net profit fell 4.7%, driven partly by the New Labour Code impact and closure of Trident Jaipur for renovation; Return on Capital Employed fell from 21.39% to 18.18% and Return on Equity fell from 18.38% to 15.31% year-on-year.
risks.risk: FY26 decline in revenue, margins and capital returns

risks.note: Temporary closure of Trident Jaipur for renovation was cited by the Company as a contributor to lower net profit in FY 2025-26, illustrating that with only seven owned hotels, taking any single property offline for capex/renovation has an outsized impact on overall results.
risks.risk: Renovation/closure-related revenue disruption in a small, concentrated hotel portfolio

risks.note: The Company's entire operations are concentrated in seven owned hotels across five Indian states (Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu) under the Oberoi Hotels & Resorts and Trident Hotels brands, so localised demand shocks, natural events or regulatory action in any one market or property can materially affect the Company.

As the Company scales its 'ITNext' AI transformation across guest-facing and back-of-house systems and predictive data architectures, the Risk Management Committee's enterprise risk framework explicitly spans business, financial, operational, environmental, reputational, legal and cyber domains, with a dedicated Chief Risk Officer overseeing the risk programme.
risks.risk: Cyber and technology risk from AI-led transformation

risks.note: The Company's identity, culture and pricing power are built entirely around membership of The Oberoi Group — operating under the licensed 'Oberoi Hotels & Resorts' and 'Trident Hotels' brands and governed by 'The Oberoi Dharma' code of conduct — making guest trust and premium positioning structurally dependent on the wider Group's brand equity and reputation.
risks.risk: Dependence on The Oberoi Group brand equity and standards
